global_research_sample.excerpt: Release Notes Node version 11.2.1 is a pre-release version of cardano-node that is not yet recommended for use on mainnet. It is a maintenance release on top of 11.2.0 . It updates to ouroboros-consensus 5.4, cardano-api 11.12 and cardano-cli 11.7, which together reduce the node's memory use around ledger snapshots, and it raises the protocol version the node advertises in block headers to 11.3. For the full set of 11.2 changes (the new cardano-config configuration format, gRPC over HTTP/2, the removal of node-to-client versions below NodeToClientV_23 , and more), see the 11.2.0 release notes . Highlights: Lower memory use. Writing a ledger snapshot no longer temporarily grows live memory by about the snapshot's size. The ChainDB also no longer keeps the genesis ledger state alive, which saves several hundred MiB on networks with a large genesis UTxO or delegation set. Faster snapshots while syncing. Description A few small nit cleanups on the synchronizer component in consensus. Behavior change: fetch_blocks_from_peers now returns as soon as no request is in flight, instead of idling until the 4s FETCH_FROM_PEERS_TIMEOUT. This affects two cases: no request was sent because every selected block was already locked, or the last outstanding request failed with no peer left to retry on. In both cases no further network request is sent, and a failed request still waits the full 2s request timeout, so periodic runs cannot repeat faster than every ~2s on failures. The only new cost is local: while all selected blocks are locked, the scheduler polls get_missing_blocks at its default 200ms cadence instead of every 4s, which is the same cadence it already uses during fast successful sync. global_research_sample.excerpt: This release contains bugfixes and improvements to the stacks-node and stacks-signer binaries, ensuring more consistent block production. This release is compatible with chainstate directories from 4.0.x. This release is recommended for all Stacks node and signer operators. This release includes the following changes: https://github.com/stacks-network/stacks-core/blob/4.0.6/CHANGELOG.md ⚠️ Breaking Changes Unused speculative tries from mining and block-proposal validation are no longer persisted. MARF databases automatically migrate to schema 4 on writable open, removing the legacy mined_blocks table and its stored tries. Older binaries cannot open upgraded databases, including in read-only mode; upgrade chainstate inspection and snapshot tooling alongside the node. Signers in this release rely on the node's new GET /v3/blocks/:block_id/view endpoint and the canonical field on /v3/sortitions to release a signed block that a Bitcoin fork has orphaned. global_research_sample.excerpt: This release removes Bitswap in favour of shrex, adds JWT token revocation, and ships a set of security and stability fixes. It is compatible with celestia-app v10 and with v0.34.x nodes on the network, so no coordinated upgrade is needed. It is recommended to upgrade. Action Recommended: run config-update This release removes the unused Share.UseShareExchange , Share.UseBitswap and Share.BlockStoreCacheSize keys from the config. Nodes start without this step and ignore the old keys. To remove them from your config.toml , stop the node, upgrade the binary and, before starting the node , run: celestia bridge config-update celestia light config-update Your custom values for the other fields are kept. Review your config.toml afterwards to confirm. Breaking changes & upgrade notes Bitswap removed: shrex is now the only share exchange protocol ( #5378 ). v0.35.0 nodes keep working with v0.34.x peers, which already used shrex first and Bitswap only as a fallback. Using the Arbitrum Platform enabled Kinetiq to configure Elysium for applications that need to update prices, manage inventory, and respond quickly as markets move.
